title: The passive, the causative, objects
subtitle: Passive forms, have/get something done, direct and indirect objects

blocks.text: Form: noun + **be** in the correct form + past participle (+ **by / with** + noun).

rows.question: am / is / are + being + past participle

rows.statement: We **asked** for water while they **were preparing** the bill.
rows.negative: We asked for water while the bill **was being prepared**.
rows.question: was / were + being + past participle

rows.statement: Someone **had eaten** all the biscuits by the time I arrived.
rows.negative: All the biscuits **had been eaten** by the time I arrived.
rows.question: had + been + past participle

rows.statement: We **will deliver** your order in twenty minutes.
rows.negative: Your order **will be delivered** in twenty minutes.
rows.question: will + be + past participle

rows.statement: Angry customers **are going to sue** the airline.
rows.negative: The airline **is going to be sued** by angry customers.
rows.question: am / is / are going to + be + past participle

rows.statement: They **will have packed** every box by Friday.
rows.negative: Every box **will have been packed** by Friday.
rows.question: will + have + been + past participle

rows.statement: You **should brush** the pastry with egg and then bake it.
rows.negative: The pastry **should be brushed** with egg and then baked.
rows.question: modal + be + past participle

rows.statement: They **should have delivered** the parcels by now.
rows.negative: The parcels **should have been delivered** by now.
rows.question: modal + have + been + past participle

rows.statement: I don't like people **telling** me what to chop in the kitchen.
rows.negative: I don't like **being told** what to chop in the kitchen.
rows.question: being + past participle

rows.use: When we do not know who does or did something
When it is obvious who does or did something
rows.example: A teenager **was arrested** last night for shoplifting.

rows.use: When it is not important who does or did something
rows.example: The old cinema **is being knocked down**.

rows.use: When we want to emphasise new information or use a more formal style
rows.example: Tomatoes **were brought** to Europe in the sixteenth century.

blocks.text: We do not normally use verbs in the passive in the present perfect continuous, past perfect continuous, future continuous or future perfect continuous. Use a different phrase instead.
blocks.note: The hotel **has been under construction** for four years. (not *has been being built*) · Dave **has been in training** as a chef for three years. (not *has been being trained*)

blocks.text: We only normally use **by** to say who did something when that person is important information.
blocks.note: The best pizzas **are made by** the Italians. (not *This steak has been overcooked by someone.*)

blocks.text: We usually use **with** when we talk about the thing used to do something.
blocks.note: The soup **should then be stirred with** a spoon. (not *stirred by a spoon*)

items: Some verbs are not normally used in the passive. They include intransitive verbs (without objects), such as **appear** and **die**, and some common transitive verbs, such as **have**, **let**, **lack**.

blocks.text: To report other people's opinions in a formal style, we can use two special forms of the passive. They work with verbs such as **say, believe, think, claim, estimate**. Some other verbs (**argue, suggest, calculate**) are usually used with only the **It is said that** structure.

items: noun + **is / are said to** + bare infinitive / perfect infinitive

rows.use: People think he is a great chef.
rows.example: He **is thought to be** a great chef. · **It is thought that** he is a great chef.

rows.use: People believe he was a great chef.
rows.example: He **is believed to have been** a great chef. · **It is believed that** he was a great chef.

rows.use: People claim she has influenced many cooks.
rows.example: She **is claimed to have had** an influence on many cooks. · **It is claimed that** she has had an influence on many other cooks.

rows.use: People say she has been making the best cheese for decades.
rows.example: She **is said to have been making** the best cheese in the area for over thirty years. · **It is said that** she has been making the best cheese in the area for over thirty years.

rows.use: People estimated that the restaurant was worth over $10 million.
rows.example: His restaurant **was estimated to be / to have been** worth over $10 million. · **It was estimated that** his restaurant was worth over $10 million.

rows.use: People have suggested that he is a great chef.
rows.example: **It has been suggested that** he is a great chef.

blocks.text: Form: noun + **have / get** in the correct form + noun + past participle (+ **by / with** + noun).

rows.use: To show that someone arranges for someone else to do something for them
rows.example: I **have my groceries delivered** by the supermarket once a week. · We **are having** a new cooker **put in** tomorrow. · We **had** a large wedding cake **made**. · **Have** you **had** your kitchen **decorated**? · We **are going to have** the food for the party **made** by a catering company.

rows.use: To refer to an unpleasant situation which hasn't been arranged
rows.example: We **had** our herb garden **vandalised** while we were away. · The Smiths **have had** their new microwave **stolen**.

blocks.text: Using the verb **get** is usually more informal than using **have**.
blocks.note: Can you go and **get** this recipe **photocopied** for me?

items: We can also use **get somebody to do** and **have somebody do** when we want to refer to the person we arrange to do something for us.
Why don't you **get the chef to prepare** you a vegetarian meal?
Why don't you **have the chef prepare** you a vegetarian meal?

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by both a direct and an indirect object (usually a person).

rows.use: Active · indirect object immediately after the verb
rows.example: A friend **gave my sister** this cookery book.

rows.use: Active · indirect object at the end with a preposition (for / to, etc.)
rows.example: A friend **gave** this cookery book **to my sister**.

rows.use: Passive · the indirect object becomes the subject
rows.example: **My sister was given** this cookery book by a friend.

rows.use: Passive · the direct object becomes the subject
rows.example: **This cookery book was given** to my sister by a friend.

exercises.title: C · Write sentences in the passive
exercises.instruction: Write a full passive sentence from the prompts. Add any extra words you need.

items.prompt: Our car / service / a mechanic / at the moment
acceptedAnswers: Our car is being serviced by a mechanic at the moment.
Our car is being serviced by a mechanic at the moment

items.prompt: A man / shoot / an air gun / outside the petrol station last night
acceptedAnswers: A man was shot with an air gun outside the petrol station last night.
A man was shot with an air gun outside the petrol station last night

items.prompt: Gunpowder / invent / the Chinese
acceptedAnswers: Gunpowder was invented by the Chinese.
Gunpowder was invented by the Chinese

items.prompt: At the surgery yesterday / I / examine / Dr Peterson / and I / give / a prescription
acceptedAnswers: At the surgery yesterday, I was examined by Dr Peterson and I was given a prescription.
At the surgery yesterday I was examined by Dr Peterson and I was given a prescription.
At the surgery yesterday, I was examined by Dr Peterson and given a prescription.

items.prompt: I went to see it because I / tell / it was a good film / all my friends
acceptedAnswers: I went to see it because I was told it was a good film by all my friends.
I went to see it because I had been told it was a good film by all my friends.
I went to see it because I was told by all my friends that it was a good film.

items.prompt: This photograph / take / my grandfather
acceptedAnswers: This photograph was taken by my grandfather.
This photograph was taken by my grandfather

items.prompt: It looked like the window / break / a hammer / some time before
acceptedAnswers: It looked like the window had been broken with a hammer some time before.
It looked like the window had been broken with a hammer some time before

items.prompt: Our dog / give / an injection / a special syringe / the vet
acceptedAnswers: Our dog was given an injection with a special syringe by the vet.
Our dog was given an injection by the vet with a special syringe.

items.prompt: The winning goal in last night's match / score / Donatello / a brilliant free kick
acceptedAnswers: The winning goal in last night's match was scored by Donatello with a brilliant free kick.
The winning goal in last night's match was scored with a brilliant free kick by Donatello.

items.prompt: Your cheque / send / last Friday and / should / deliver / to you tomorrow
acceptedAnswers: Your cheque was sent last Friday and should be delivered to you tomorrow.
Your cheque was sent last Friday and it should be delivered to you tomorrow.

exercises.title: E · Impersonal passive
exercises.instruction: Rewrite in the passive, starting with the words given.

items.prompt:
People say that Bali is a beautiful island.
**It**
acceptedAnswers: It is said that Bali is a beautiful island.
It is said that Bali is a beautiful island

items.prompt:
People generally think that life won't be found on Mars.
**It**
acceptedAnswers: It is generally thought that life won't be found on Mars.
It is generally thought that life won't be found on Mars
It is generally thought that life will not be found on Mars.

items.prompt:
It is generally said that Christmas is too commercialised.
**Christmas**
acceptedAnswers: Christmas is generally said to be too commercialised.
Christmas is generally said to be too commercialised

items.prompt:

**It**
acceptedAnswers: It is often argued that prison doesn't work.
It is often argued that prison doesn't work
It is often argued that prison does not work.

items.prompt:
People have suggested that the school should start to produce a magazine.
**It**
acceptedAnswers: It has been suggested that the school should start to produce a magazine.
It has been suggested that the school should start to produce a magazine

items.prompt:
People say that crocodile tastes like squid.
**Crocodile**
acceptedAnswers: Crocodile is said to taste like squid.
Crocodile is said to taste like squid

items.prompt:
It is said that the Vikings discovered America before Columbus.
**The Vikings**
acceptedAnswers: The Vikings are said to have discovered America before Columbus.

items.prompt:

acceptedAnswers: Heart disease is thought to be caused by eating the wrong things.
